'''Mark Andrew Thomson''' (born 28 April 1966) is a British particle physicist. He is a Professor of Experimental Particle Physics at the [[Cavendish Laboratory]] at the [[University of Cambridge]] and a Fellow at [[Emmanuel College, Cambridge]]. From January 2018 to December 2024, he was the Executive Chair of the [[Science and Technology Facilities Council]], one of the nine councils of [[UK Research and Innovation]].<ref name=stfc>{{cite web|title=New STFC Executive Chair announced - Science and Technology Facilities Council|url=https://www.stfc.ac.uk/news/new-stfc-executive-chair-announced/|website=stfc.ac.uk|date=22 January 2018|language=en}}</ref><ref name=home>{{cite web|title=Mark Thomson's Home Page|url=http://www.hep.phy.cam.ac.uk/~thomson/|website=hep.phy.cam.ac.uk|accessdate=23 January 2018|language=en}}</ref> Thomson was a delegate of the [[United Kingdom]] to the [[CERN]] Council,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://council.web.cern.ch/en/content/council-composition-january-2024|title=Council - Composition as from January 2024}}</ref> the [[Square Kilometre Array]] Observatory (SKAO)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.manchester.ac.uk/discover/news/uk-to-build-software-brain-for-giant-radio-telescope/|title=UK to build software brain for giant radio telescope}}</ref> and [[European Spallation Source]] ERIC (ESS).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://europeanspallationsource.se/ess-organisation/governance|title=Governance}}</ref> Thomson was appointed director-general of CERN on 1 January 2026.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Castelvecchi |first=Davide |date=2024-11-07 |title=New CERN chief pledges to forge ahead with $17-billion supercollider |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-024-03666-x |journal=Nature |language=en |doi=10.1038/d41586-024-03666-x |issn=0028-0836|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://home.cern/news/press-release/cern/cern-council-selects-mark-thomson-next-director-general-starting-2026|title=CERN Council selects Mark Thomson as next Director-General, starting in 2026}}</ref>

==Education==
Thomson was educated at [[Worthing College|Worthing Sixth Form College]] where he completed [[A-level]]s in Mathematics, Further Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry.<ref name=cv/> Thomson completed a [[Bachelor of Arts degree]] in Physics in 1988 and a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] degree in 1991 on Experimental Physics at the [[University of Oxford]] supervised by John Henry Cobb.<ref name=dphil>{{cite thesis |degree=DPhil |first=Mark Andrew|last=Thomson |title=An experimental study of the possible association of deep underground muons with astronomical point sources |publisher=University of Oxford |date=1991 |url=https://solo.bodleian.ox.ac.uk/permalink/44OXF_INST/35n82s/alma990121465360107026 |website=ox.ac.uk |oclc= 863481031 |doi= |hdl=}}</ref><ref name=home/><ref name=cv>{{Cite web|url=http://www.hep.phy.cam.ac.uk/~thomson/cv_mark_thomson.pdf|title=Professor Mark Thomson CV|last=Thomson|first=Mark|website=cam.ac.uk|year=2017}}</ref><ref name=cobb>{{cite web|url=https://www.keble.ox.ac.uk/alumni-friends/life-stories/life-stories-john-henry-cobb-1968/|title=John Henry Cobb (1968 BA DPhil Physics) died on 29 July 2024 aged 75 after a short Illness|website=keble.ox.ac.uk|publisher=University of Oxford}}</ref>

==Research and career==
From 1992 to 1994, Thomson was a [[postdoctoral research]] [[fellow]] in the High Energy Physics group at [[University College London]]. In 1994, he joined CERN firstly as a fellow and then as a staff research physicist where he worked on the [[OPAL experiment]]. Since 2000, Thomson has worked at the University of Cambridge as a [[Lecturer]] (2000–2004), [[Reader (academic rank)|Reader]] (2004–2008) and [[Professor]] of Experimental Particle Physics (2008–present).<ref name=home/>

From 2015 to 2018, Thomson was the co-leader and co-spokesperson for the [[Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment]] (DUNE) in the United States.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/science/life-and-physics/2017/sep/24/uk-invests-65m-in-deep-underground-neutrino-experiment-in-us|title=UK invests £65m in Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment in US|website=theguardian.com|publisher=[[The Guardian]] |date=24 September 2017 |last1=Butterworth |first1=Jon }}</ref> Thomson also worked on [[MicroBooNE]]<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/mundo/vert-earth-59079004|title=Neutrino estéril: el experimento fallido que abre un nuevo capítulo en la búsqueda del origen del universo|newspaper=BBC News Mundo }}</ref> and the [[MINOS]]<ref>{{cite book|chapter-url=https://www.worldscientific.com/doi/abs/10.1142/9789813227460_0028?download=true|chapter=A Personal Journey from MINOS to DUNE|doi=10.1142/9789813227460_0028 |title=Fermilab at 50 |date=2017 |last1=Thomson |first1=Mark |pages=96–98 |isbn=978-981-322-745-3 }}</ref> experiments.

In 2026, Thomson was appointed [[List of honorary fellows of Pembroke College, Oxford|Honorary Fellow at Pembroke College Oxford]].

===Publications===

Thomson is the author or co-author of more than 1100 publications in [[peer reviewed]] scientific journals covering a number of major areas in High Energy Particle Physics.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://inspirehep.net/authors/986155?ui-citation-summary=true|title=Mark Andrew Thomson}}</ref> His main research interests are in electron-positron collider physics, neutrino physics and the development of novel and powerful reconstruction techniques for cutting edge detector technologies. In addition to his research activities, he is the author of the textbook "Modern Particle Physics".<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://www.cambridge.org/highereducation/books/modern-particle-physics/CDFEBC9AE513DA60AA12DE015181A948#overview|title=Modern Particle Physics|date=2013 |doi=10.1017/CBO9781139525367 |last1=Thomson |first1=Mark |isbn=978-1-107-03426-6 |publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]]|oclc=}}</ref>
